How much interest is earned in the first two years?

parts.latex:
An amount of \$25 000 is invested for six years. Interest is earned at a rate of $8\%$ per annum, compounding quarterly.

Which expression gives the value of the investment after 6 years, in dollars?

solutions.latex:
Interest compounds quarterly, so there are 4 periods per year.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{rate per quarter} &= \dfrac{8\%}{4} = 2\% = 0.02\\ \text{number of quarters} &= 6\times 4 = 24 \end{aligned}$$
Using $A = P(1+r)^n$:
$$A = 25\,000\times 1.02^{24}$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
Alex purchased 800 shares. The total cost was \$2.60 per share. Alex sold the shares one year later for \$3.40 each and paid a fee of \$24.95 for selling the shares.

What profit did Alex make on these shares?

solutions.latex:
Profit is the selling amount, less the fee, less the cost.

Cost of the shares:
$$800 \times 2.60 = \$2080$$
Amount received from the sale:
$$800 \times 3.40 = \$2720$$
The selling fee is subtracted:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Profit} &= 2720 - 24.95 - 2080 \\ &= \$615.05 \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

parts.latex:
In ten years, the future value of an investment will be \$150 000. The interest rate is $4\%$ per annum, compounded half-yearly.

Which equation will give the present value ($PV$) of the investment?

solutions.latex:
The present value formula is $PV = \dfrac{FV}{(1+r)^n}$, where $r$ is the interest rate per compounding period and $n$ is the number of periods.

Compounded half-yearly, there are 2 periods each year:
$$r = \dfrac{0.04}{2} = 0.02, \qquad n = 10 \times 2 = 20$$
Hence
$$PV = \dfrac{150\,000}{(1+0.02)^{20}}$$
This is option D.
